# parse { #labdata.manifest.parse }

```python
labdata.manifest.parse(text, directory)
```

Read a manifest.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**text**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Content of the ``labdata.yml`` file.

<code>[**directory**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative directory the manifest sits in, used to make its keys relative and to report where a problem is.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Manifest](`labdata.manifest.Manifest`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The parsed manifest. An empty ``files`` mapping is allowed and publishes nothing.

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ManifestError](`labdata.manifest.ManifestError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If the file is not valid YAML, has no ``files`` mapping, gives an entry a value that is neither a description nor a mapping holding one, or names a file with a key that climbs out of the directory with ``..``.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
parse("files:\n  hits.csv: candidate hits\n", "results")
# Manifest(directory='results', files={'hits.csv': 'candidate hits'})
```
